title: WPPIL/108/2012 of MOHTAREEM Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (PIL) No. 108 of 2012
With
Review Application No. 1526 of 2017
Delay Condonation Application No.18205 of 2018
Mohtareem .......Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others .......Respondents
None appears for the petitioner.
Mr. M.S. Tyagi, Advocate for the review applicants.
Mr. S.S. Chauhan, Deputy Advocate General for the State.
Mr. Ajay Veer Pundir, Advocate for the respondent no.7.
Coram: Hon'ble Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.
 Hon'ble Lok Pal Singh, J.
 The order, review of which is sought, is the order passed in
Writ Petition (PIL) No.108 of 2012 dated 19.06.2018, wherein the following
mandatory directions were issued:-
i. The Chief Secretary to the State of Uttarakhand is directed to take
disciplinary action against the persons who were indicted for the
change of revenue entries, even against those who have retired or
transferred.
ii. State Government is directed to re-claim government land from
the encroachers.
iii. The Secretary, Revenue is directed to ensure that the river course
is restored to its original course to save the villages downstream.
iv. A Special Investigating Team is constituted to implement the
report dated 18.06.2014 headed by Mr. Krishan Kumar V.K.,
S.S.P. Haridwar, to be assisted by S.P. City Haridwar in order to
lodge the F.I.Rs. against the Officers under the relevant provisions
of the Indian Penal Code and Prevention of Corruption Act.
v. Needful be done by the concerned authorities within a period of
three months from today.
2. The applicants have now sought review of the order passed in
Writ Petition (PIL) No.108 of 2012 dated 19.06.2018, contending that, in
view of the aforesaid order passed by the Division Bench, lands allotted to
them as a measure of consolidation are now sought to be taken away without
their even being given back the fragmented and divided extents of land
which was taken away from them in exchange for the consolidated land
given to them.
3. While fairly stating that a part of the land, allotted to them, is
recorded in the Revenue records as river bed land, and river bed land cannot
be allotted as a measure of consolidation, Mr. M.S. Tyagi, learned counsel
for the review applicants, would submit that the order passed by the

2
authorities, under the U.P. Consolidation of Holding Act, 1953, has attained
finality; and unless it is reopened by a judicial order from this Court, the
applicants would be left with no other remedy. He would also state that the
applicants have already raised a wheat crop on the land which is ripe for
harvesting; and they be permitted to harvest the wheat crop raised on the
subject land.
4. Various factual aspects have been pleaded, for the first time, in
the affidavit filed in support of the review application. All these aspects can
only be examined after the State Government files its counter-affidavit in
reply thereto. Suffice it, for the present, if the applicants are permitted to
harvest the wheat crop raised on the subject land on condition that they shall
not commence agricultural activities hereafter till the review applications are
finally heard and decided.
5. The review applicants can, at best, claim to be aggrieved by the
Direction No.2 of the order under review. It is not known whether the other
directions issued by the Division Bench, in its order in Writ Petition (PIL)
No.108 of 2012 dated 19.06.2018, have been complied with or not.
6. While filing its counter-affidavit to the review application, the
State Government shall also inform this Court as to what action has been
taken by them in compliance with the other directions issued by the Division
Bench in its order in Writ Petition (PIL) No.108 of 2012 dated 19.06.2018.
7. Mr. S.S. Chauhan, learned Deputy Advocate General for the
State, requests three weeks' time to file counter-affidavit.
8. Post after three weeks.
 (Lok Pal Singh, J.) (Ramesh Ranganathan, C. J.)
 17.05.2019 17.05.2019
NISHANT
